title: Minimum Score Triangulation of Polygon
statement:
A convex polygon has `n` corners, listed clockwise, and corner `i` carries the integer label `values[i]`. A triangulation splits the polygon into triangles using only diagonals between its own corners, so that no other shapes remain; every triangulation produces exactly `n - 2` triangles.

Each triangle costs the product of the labels at its three corners, and a triangulation costs the sum of its triangles' costs. Return the smallest cost that any triangulation of the polygon can have.
notes:
## Intuition

Look at the side joining the first and last corners, `0` and `n - 1`. In any triangulation it belongs to exactly one triangle, whose third corner is some `k` between them. That triangle splits the polygon into two smaller polygons: corners `0..k` and corners `k..n-1`, which are triangulated independently. So the best cost for a run of consecutive corners `i..j` depends only on the best costs of shorter runs. Trying every triangulation directly is exponential (Catalan many), but there are only O(n²) runs.

## Approach

1. Let `dp[i][j]` be the cheapest triangulation of the polygon made by corners `i, i+1, ..., j`. Runs of two corners (a single side) cost `0`.
2. Fill runs in order of increasing `length = j - i`, from 2 up to `n - 1`.
3. For each run, try every middle corner `k` with `i < k < j` as the apex of the triangle on side `i`–`j`: its cost is `dp[i][k] + dp[k][j] + values[i] * values[k] * values[j]`.
4. Keep the minimum in `dp[i][j]` and return `dp[0][n - 1]`.

## Example 1, step by step

`values = [1, 2, 3]`, so `n = 3`. Only `length = 2` is processed, with `i = 0`, `j = 2`. The single choice `k = 1` gives `score = dp[0][1] + dp[1][2] + 1 * 2 * 3 = 0 + 0 + 6 = 6`, so `dp[0][2] = 6` is returned.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n³): O(n²) runs, each trying up to n apexes.
- Space: O(n²) for `dp`.

## Pitfalls

- Fill by run length, not by `i` from 0 upward; `dp[i][k]` and `dp[k][j]` must already be final.
- Runs of two corners cost 0, not `Infinity`; only runs of three or more have triangles.
- Greedily cutting off the cheapest ear first is not optimal; all splits must be compared.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | number of corners |
| `dp[i][j]` | cheapest triangulation of corners `i..j` |
| `length` | `j - i`, the size of the run being solved |
| `i`, `j` | first and last corner of the run |
| `k` | apex of the triangle on side `i`–`j` |
| `score` | cost of the run when `k` is the apex |

narration.3: dp[i][j] is the cheapest triangulation of corners i..j; runs of two corners stay 0.
narration.4: Solve runs in order of length so shorter runs are always ready.
narration.5: Slide the run's first corner i along the polygon.
narration.6: The run ends at corner j.
narration.7: Start with no known triangulation for this run.
narration.8: Try each corner k between i and j as the apex of the triangle on side i-j.
narration.9: That triangle plus the best triangulations of the two pieces it leaves.
narration.10: Keep the cheapest choice of apex.
narration.14: The whole polygon is the run from corner 0 to corner n - 1.
